'''Dirk Ahrens''' (born 1971) is a German biologist and taxonomist at the [[Museum Koenig]] (Zoological Research Museum Alexander Koenig) in [[Bonn]], Germany. He specializes in [[scarab beetles]] (Scarabaeidae) and became curator of the museum's Coleoptera section on 1 May 2010.<ref name="Jahresbericht2010">{{cite report |title=Annual Report 2010 |publisher=Zoological Research Museum Alexander Koenig |url=https://www.zfmk.de/dateien/dokumente/zfmk_jahresbericht2010.pdf#page=102 |format=PDF |access-date=4 February 2018}}</ref>

== Biography ==

Ahrens studied biology at the [[University of Greifswald]], specializing in zoology and ecology. He graduated with a diploma in 1997 and subsequently worked as a research associate at the State Museum of Zoology in [[Dresden]].<ref name="Jahresbericht2010"/>

From 2001 to 2004, he pursued doctoral research at the German Entomological Institute in [[Eberswalde]], receiving his doctoral degree from the [[Free University of Berlin]]. In 2005, he worked for [[Helvetas]], a Swiss development cooperation organization. From 2006 to 2008, he was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Museum of Natural History, Munich|Natural History Museum in Munich]]. In 2010, he joined the Zoological Research Museum Alexander Koenig in Bonn.<ref name="Jahresbericht2010"/>

His research interests include the [[molecular systematics]] of beetles, evolutionary biology, and [[integrative taxonomy]]. According to the museum's 2010 annual report, his scientific publications had described nearly 500 new species.<ref name="Jahresbericht2010"/>

== Selected publications ==

Ahrens has published monographs, book chapters, and scientific journal articles. A publication list is available on the museum's website.<ref name="Publications">{{cite web |title=Dirk Ahrens: Publications |publisher=Zoological Research Museum Alexander Koenig |url=https://www.zfmk.de/de/zfmk/dirk-ahrens#pub |access-date=4 February 2018}}</ref>

* Timmermans, M. J. T. N.; Dodsworth, S.; Culverwell, C. L.; Bocak, L.; Ahrens, D.; Littlewood, D. T. J.; Pons, J.; Vogler, A. P. (2010). "Why barcode? High-throughput multiplex sequencing of mitochondrial genomes for molecular systematics". ''[[Nucleic Acids Research]]'', pp. 1–14.
* Keith, D.; Rössner, E.; Ahrens, D. (2010). "Zur Identität von ''[[Triodontella alni]]'' (Blanchard, 1850) und ''Serica luteipes'' Fairmaire, 1881 (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae, Sericini)". ''Entomologische Zeitschrift'', 120, pp. 103–107.
* Rössner, E.; Scheuern, J.; Ahrens, D. (2010). "Onthophagus (Palaeonthophagus) medius (Kugelann, 1792)—a good western Palaearctic species in the Onthophagus vacca complex (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae: Scarabaeinae: Onthophagini)". ''[[Zootaxa]]'', 2629, pp. 1–28.
* Ahrens, D.; Gc, Y. D.; Lago, P. K.; Nagel, P. (2009). "Seasonal fluctuation, phenology and turnover of chafer assemblages—insight into the structural plasticity of insect communities in tropical farmland (Coleoptera: Scarabaeidae)". ''Agricultural and Forest Entomology'', 11, pp. 265–274.
* Ahrens, D.; Fabrizi, S. (2009). "New species of [[Sericini]] from the Eastern Himalaya and Tibet (Coleoptera, Scarabaeidae)". In: Hartmann, M.; Weipert, M. (eds.), ''Biodiversity and Natural Heritage of the Himalaya III''. Verein der Freunde und Förderer des Naturkundemuseums Erfurt e.V., Erfurt, pp. 249–284.
* Ahrens, D. (2006). "Sericinae". In: Löbl, I.; Smetana, A. (eds.), ''Catalogue of the Palaearctic Coleoptera''. Apollo Books, pp. 229–248.
* Ahrens, D. (2005). ''A taxonomic review on the Serica (s. str.) MacLeay, 1819 species of Asiatic mainland (Coleoptera, Scarabaeidae, Sericini)''. Nova Supplementa Entomologica, 18, pp. 1–163.
* Rössner, E.; Ahrens, D. (2004). ''Taxonomie und Chorologie der Gattung Omaloplia, Schoenherr, 1817 (Insecta, Coleoptera, Melolonthidae, Sericini)''. dissertation.de, Berlin.
* Ahrens, D.; Assing, V.; Bellmann, A.; Bellstedt, R.; Eisinger, D.; Esser, J.; Frank, J.; Geider, R.; Gürlich, S.; Hartmann, M.; Klausnitzer, B.; Klinger, R.; Köhler, F.; Konzelmann, E.; Möller, G.; Schmidt, L.; Schnitter, P.; Spitzenberg, D.; Sprick, P.; Terlutter, H.
